title: Planning ahead
respondents: People we support who had an advance care planning conversation with us, or with our contribution, 4 to 8 weeks ago; never someone who declined or stopped it; asked by phone or face to face only
summary: A gentle phone or face-to-face check, 4 to 8 weeks after an advance care planning conversation, that it was offered well: at a good time, with the right people, without pressure, with a copy and care workers who know. About 10 minutes.
purpose: Asks living people whether the advance care planning conversation the End of Life Care Policy promises was offered well: at a time they chose, with the people they wanted, without pressure, told about choosing someone to decide for them and about changing their wishes, recorded, copied to them and known by their care workers. It is the 'before' measure that matches the bereaved family survey (SUR-FAM-002). Results go to the Registered Manager and the staff trained in advance care planning, feed training and the policy's monitoring of advance care planning offered and recorded, and check each person's wishes are recorded correctly. A gate question lets the person decline the whole topic without a reason.

timing.when: 4 to 8 weeks after an advance care planning conversation recorded in CareFlow; never after one the person declined or stopped, and never in the last weeks of life unless they ask
timing.trigger: An advance care planning conversation recorded in the care plan, held by us or with our contribution

introduction:
This call from {{organisation}} is about the conversation we had with you about planning for the future. It takes about 10 minutes, and you can stop at any time. You do not have to talk about it if you would rather not.

What you say will not affect your care. Your answers are linked to your name so we can make sure your wishes are recorded the way you want. Your care workers (carers) will not see your answers.

This survey is not for urgent concerns. If you are worried about your safety or someone else's, or need help now, phone the office (out of hours, the on-call number in your care folder). In an emergency, call 999.
privacyNotice:
{{organisation}} uses your answers to check we plan ahead with you well and to improve our care. Our legal reason is our legitimate interest in running a good, safe service. Health details stay confidential.

Your answers are linked to your name so we can put things right. They are seen only by our Registered Manager and Care Coordinators, never by your care workers (carers), and reports show combined results only. If you tell us a new wish, we record it in your care plan with your agreement. If you tell us someone may be at risk of harm, we may tell the council to keep them safe.

We keep your answers for 3 years after this survey, under our Records Management and Retention Policy. You can ask to see, correct or delete your answers, or object to our using them, by contacting the office or our Data Protection Officer (details on our website). You can also complain to the Information Commission.

questions.text: Overall, how was your experience of our service?
questions.helpText: Please think about your care over the last few months. Choose "Don't know" if you are not sure.

comment.prompt: Please tell us why you gave this answer.

questions.text: Some questions are about planning for the future, including the end of life. Is it all right to talk about this today?
questions.helpText: If the person says not today, close the form without saving (a saved answer would stop the later call being recorded), note it on the call list and offer another time within the next 4 weeks. If they would rather not talk about this, choose that answer, thank them, save and end kindly.
options: No, I would rather not talk about this

questions.text: Did we talk with you about the future at a time that suited you?
Were the people you wanted involved in the conversation?
options: I did not want anyone else involved
notCountedOptions: I did not want anyone else involved

comment.prompt: Who would you have liked to involve?

questions.text: Did you feel able to say as much or as little as you wanted?
questions.evidence: Effective: Consent to care and treatment

questions.text: Did we tell you that you can choose someone to make decisions for you, if one day you cannot?
questions.helpText: This means a lasting power of attorney. We only tell people about it; we never help write or witness one. Do not ask whether the person has one.

questions.text: Do you know you can change your wishes at any time?
Do you have a copy of what you told us, in a way you can read or use?
options: I did not want a copy
notCountedOptions: I did not want a copy

questions.text: Do your care workers know what matters to you for the future?

comment.prompt: What do they need to know?

questions.text: Is there anything else about your wishes for the future that you would like us to know or do?
questions.helpText: Write the person's own words. A new or changed wish is passed to the Care Coordinator today to be recorded.

questions.text: Would you like someone to contact you about your answers?
questions.helpText: If the person says Yes, someone from our office, not one of their care workers, will contact them within 5 working days.

howToRun: Ask by phone or face to face only: never send this survey to the portal, by post or as a link, and never use Send or schedule for it (that would put it in the person's portal). Start one copy from this template and use Open for responses; enter each call or visit with Record response (channel Telephone or In person). Keep a list of advance care planning conversations recorded in care plans and when this call is due, 4 to 8 weeks later (CareFlow has no event triggers yet).

Never ask someone who declined or stopped the planning conversation: the End of Life Care Policy says we offer it again only at the next full review or if they raise it. Never ask in the last weeks of life (an end of life plan in place) unless the person asks. Phone first to ask if it is a good time. Before calling, check the person's survey history in CareFlow: only if they have had no other survey in the last 4 weeks; this call counts as their survey contact for the next 4 weeks.

By default only managers and admins can record survey answers ("Record survey responses") and only managers can open a survey for responses: give both to the staff who make these calls. The caller is a Field Care Supervisor, Care Coordinator, Deputy Manager or Registered Manager trained in advance care planning, not the person who held the conversation and not in the core care team. Use a professional interpreter, never family.

Listen, do not advise. If the person cannot take part, do not ask a family member instead: family views come through the family survey (SUR-FAM-001) or, after a death, the bereaved family survey (SUR-FAM-002). For people living with dementia, use plain words and picture cards if they help. If the person becomes upset, stop, offer support and tell the Care Coordinator the same day. This survey never asks about resuscitation decisions or ReSPECT plans.

Who may open individual answers: the staff trained in advance care planning who make the calls, the Care Coordinator and the Registered Manager. This is set in Who can see the answers: individual responses are limited to Care Coordinators and the Registered Manager, and results to Care Coordinators, the Registered Manager and the Deputy Manager, showing from 5 answers. Super Admin, Admin and the person who made the survey can always see both, so keep those roles to staff who may open them. Add the role of the staff trained in advance care planning who make the calls.
actingOnResults: Act on every answer that needs it the same working day, under the alerts below. A new wish is not survey data: it goes into the care plan through the Care Coordinator.

How to count: report the share answering Yes to each question, leaving out Don't know and the "did not want" answers; report how many people would rather not talk about it, and, from the call list, how many said not today. Numbers will be small: report once a year, never report a group of fewer than 5 people separately, and flag results resting on fewer than 10.

The Registered Manager reviews the results with the staff trained in advance care planning and uses them in training and in the End of Life Care Policy's monitoring of advance care planning offered and recorded. Compare them with the bereaved family survey's answers on whether wishes were known and respected. Actions go into the service improvement plan within 5 working days under the Governance and Quality Assurance Policy.

Keep answers for 3 years after the survey closes under the Records Management and Retention Policy. For CQC, these answers show people are supported to plan for the future in their own way (Regulations 9 and 17(2)(e)).

alerts.when: Any new or changed wish in any answer.
alerts.action: Pass it to the Care Coordinator the same working day; a trained colleague records it in the person's words, gives the person a copy in their format within 5 working days and, with their agreement, sends a summary to the GP practice and community nursing team within 2 working days, under the End of Life Care Policy. A wish to refuse treatment in advance is referred to the GP the same working day; our staff never draft or witness one.

alerts.when: Any mention of wanting to end their life.
alerts.action: Listen without judgement and never help or advise; tell the office the same day. The Registered Manager makes sure the GP knows within 1 working day, and any risk of self-harm is handled at once under the Safeguarding Adults Policy.

alerts.when: "Did you feel able to say as much or as little as you wanted?" answered No, or a comment suggesting pressure, including from family, to choose a particular outcome.
alerts.action: Tell the Registered Manager the same working day. If coercion or undue influence is suggested, tell the safeguarding lead the same working day; the risk is assessed within 1 hour of the report under the Safeguarding Concerns: Reporting, Referral and Enquiry Procedure, and an independent advocate is considered. Otherwise the Care Coordinator contacts the person within 5 working days.

rule.task: Could not say what they wanted: check for pressure

alerts.when: "Do you have a copy of what you told us?" answered No.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator sends a copy in the person's format within 5 working days.

rule.task: Send a copy of their wishes in their format

alerts.when: "Do your care workers know what matters to you for the future?" answered No.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator updates the care plan summary and tells every rostered care worker before their next visit.

rule.task: Update care plan summary and brief care workers

alerts.when: A good time, the right people, being told about choosing someone to decide or about changing wishes answered No, or the overall question Poor or Very poor.
alerts.action: The Care Coordinator contacts the person within 5 working days to agree what we will do; the Registered Manager uses the pattern in advance care planning training.

rule.task: Planning conversation fell short: follow up

alerts.when: The person becomes upset during the call.
alerts.action: Stop, offer support and tell the Care Coordinator the same day; the Care Coordinator contacts the person within 1 working day (our recommendation; the policy sets no timescale).

alerts.when: "Is it all right to talk about this today?" answered No, I would rather not talk about this.
alerts.action: Record in the call notes that the person did not want to answer this survey, and do not ask again for this conversation. This is not a decline of advance care planning itself.

rule.task: Did not want to answer: note it, do not ask again

if.question: q-ok
answers: No, I would rather not talk about this

alerts.action: Record a complaint the same working day; it is graded within 1 working day and acknowledged within 3 working days, under the Complaints Policy and Procedure.

alerts.when: "Would you like someone to contact you about your answers?" answered Yes.
alerts.action: Office staff contact the person within 5 working days and record what was agreed.

rule.task: Asked to be contacted about their answers

regulatoryBasis.source: NHS England, Universal Principles for Advance Care Planning (March 2022): the person is central; personalised conversations; a shareable plan; the chance to review and revise it
Mental Capacity Act 2005, sections 9 to 14 (lasting powers of attorney) and 24 to 26 (advance decisions to refuse treatment)
Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Regulation 9(3): person-centred care, including enabling people to make or take part in decisions about their care
Health and Social Care Act 2008 (Regulated Activities) Regulations 2014, Regulation 17(2)(e): seek and act on feedback
